decisions.reason: The archiving and reporting software has its own web page and is central to the firm's announced move toward data-driven infrastructure management, so its visible commitment and strategic fit argue for persisting with it.

This second archiving software is only mentioned on the website and partly overlaps with A, so the firm could consolidate it at little cost, but it still fits the digital direction and is likely kept for now.

The manhole floor door has a dedicated page and builds on the firm's established hardware, so public commitment and sunk development effort favour keeping it while results can still be blamed on early market ramp-up.
The floating sludge extractor is only mentioned, so little would need justifying if it were dropped, but it extends the core wastewater machinery line and is plausibly kept for its niche customers.

The control technology for water engineering machinery ties the firm's proprietary machines to its automation offer, which supports its integrated-solution strategy, so dropping it would undermine the announced direction.
